whatIsIt.eli5: Stacks two piles of notes about the same spots into one taller pile.
whatIsIt.simple: Joins maps of the same height and width by stacking their channels. A 256-channel map and a 128-channel map become one 384-channel map.
whatIsIt.engineer: torch.cat(xs, dim=1); requires equal H×W; output channels = Σ inputs; no params or MACs.

whyExists.eli5: It lets the model use both detailed notes and big-picture notes together.
whyExists.simple: This is how the neck combines features from different depths: detailed but simple features from the backbone with deeper, more meaningful ones. The next block learns how to mix them.
whyExists.engineer: Lateral fusion in PAN-FPN; concatenation (vs. addition) keeps both sources intact and lets the following C2f/C3k2 learn the mixing.

eli5: Check both maps are the same size.
Put one pile on top of the other.
simple: All inputs must have the same height and width.
Channels are placed one after another.
Nothing is learned here; the next block does the mixing.
engineer: Concat with mismatched spatial size is the most common error after editing; fix with Upsample or a stride-2 Conv.

example.eli5: A pile of 256 notes plus a pile of 128 notes makes a pile of 384.
example.simple: YOLOv8n layer 11 joins the upsampled 256×40×40 map with backbone layer 6 (128×40×40) → 384×40×40.

typicalPositions.eli5: Wherever two paths meet in the mixing part.
typicalPositions.simple: Every fusion point of the neck, both top-down and bottom-up.
